name: Lugh
loreTies: Source: Morrígan (battle crow, fate, war prophecy)
shortBackstory: Lugh is the granite-bough breaker — the Morrígan-source whose battle-crow prophecy foretells who will fall and then ensures the prophecy is fulfilled.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Lugh was born from the battle-crow — the omen that appears before slaughter. He is the breaker who shatters what fate has marked for breaking. Ancient humans saw the Morrígan — but they saw the prophecy and missed the purpose. Lugh ensures the worthy fall well and the unworthy fall first.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Among the Tuatha, Lugh knows who will survive before the battle begins. His battle-crow sight reads fate on the battlefield. He does not build or renew; he ends, and the ending is always what fate was leaning toward.

chapters.title: Gate Wound
chapters.text: The Mythos Gate wounded Lugh by making his prophecies false. The Hollow removed warriors he had marked for death — not by saving them but by erasing them. His battle-crow sight showed deaths for beings who no longer existed.

chapters.title: Campaign Role
chapters.text: In Roots Below the Gate, Lugh shatters enemies marked by fate. His granite-bough maul channels battle-crow prophecy into destruction. But the Hollow makes his prophecies unreliable — he marks enemies who have already been erased.

chapters.title: Personal Conflict
chapters.text: Lugh's flaw is that he has never questioned fate. He accepts what he sees as inevitable. The Hollow teaches him that some 'inevitabilities' are not fate — they are erasure, and treating erasure as fate means abandoning beings who could have been saved.

relationshipHooks: Cross-faction envoys can challenge their doctrine without erasing their faction identity.
developmentStatus: Readable profile integrated into dashboard character pages.
human_echo: Lugh's harvest festival (Lughnasadh) was a human echo of his real skill-mastery
